title: Memory Performance and Power Modeling Intern
description: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. As an AI/ML Workload Analysis Intern , you will work with system architects and performance engineers to analyze emerging AI workloads and evaluate next-generation computing and memory architecture. You will develop methodologies to characterize memory behavior, generate workload traces, and uncover performance bottlenecks across AI training and inference applications. You will develop insights into how large language models (LLMs), recommendation systems, vision models, and multimodal AI applications interact with CPUs, GPUs, NPUs, memory subsystems, and interconnects. You will leverage simulation, profiling, and data analysis tools to study performance bottlenecks, memory behavior, bandwidth requirements, and scalability characteristics of AI workloads. The focus of this role is on memory trace-based workload analysis , helping drive architectural decisions for future memory technologies and AI platforms. You will work with real-world AI workloads, trace collection tools, and analytics frameworks to understand memory access patterns, bandwidth demands, cache efficiency, data movement, and system bottlenecks. Responsibilities Analyze AI/ML workloads including Large Language Models (LLMs), recommendation models, computer vision, multimodal, and generative AI applications. Collect, process, and analyze memory traces from AI training and inference workloads. Characterize memory access patterns, locality, reuse behavior, bandwidth utilization, and latency sensitivity. Characterize compute, memory, storage, and interconnect behavior across AI training and inference workloads. Develop workload traces, performance models, and architecture simulation environments. Investigate system bottlenecks related to memory capacity, bandwidth, latency, cache utilization, and communication overheads. Evaluate architectural tradeoffs across CPUs, GPUs, NPUs, accelerators, and memory technologies. Create automation frameworks for workload execution, data collection, and results analysis. Validate simulation and analytical models using benchmark and hardware measurements. Present findings through technical reports, visualizations, and architecture reviews. Minimum Qualifications Pursuing an MS or PhD in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Data Science, or a related field. Coursework or research experience in: Computer Architecture Machine Learning / Deep Learning Parallel Computing Operating Systems Data Structures and Algorithms Performance Analysis Programming experience in: Python C/C++ Strong analytical, problem-solving, and quantitative reasoning skills. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Preferred Qualifications Experience with AI frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX, or ONNX. Familiarity with LLMs, transformers, diffusion models, recommender systems, or vision models. Experience with workload profiling, tracing, or performance analysis tools. Experience with simulation, modeling, or architecture research is a plus. Experience with AI code assistant is a plus Experience with performance profiling tools such as Nsight, VTune, perf, rocprof, or similar tools. Knowledge of GPU, NPU, TPU, or accelerator architectures. Understanding of memory systems, including cache hierarchies, DRAM. Experience with architecture simulators such as Gem5, Accel-Sim, or similar tools. Familiarity with Linux development environments and data analysis frameworks. title: Electrical Design Automation Intern - AI & EDA Automation
Embedded Software Engineer Intern
description: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. Join Our Team as an Embedded Systems Software Engineer Intern Micron Technology Inc. is a global leader in semiconductor manufacturing. The Systems Integration Group (SIG) designs and manufactures internal equipment to give Micron a competitive position in the marketplace. Our Equipment Software Design team is looking for a hands-on Embedded Systems Software Engineering Intern who enjoys working at the intersection of software, electronics, and complete system behavior. This intern will develop embedded software running on bare metal and embedded Linux as well as higher level interface software. You will work with other software engineers and other engineering fields to develop custom in-house semiconductor equipment from the ground up. This role requires an understanding of hardware behavior to build, debug, and optimize software that directly controls custom electronic systems. This is not a purely software role. Successful candidates will have a foundation in both software and electronics and should enjoy understanding how the complete system works. You will routinely move between source code, device registers, schematics, datasheets, electrical signals, and lab equipment while developing and debugging systems. Responsibilities Design, develop, test, and support embedded software in C, C++, Bash, and Python for bare-metal and RHEL-compatible Linux environments, including containerized applications. Collaborate with software, electrical, controls, and mechanical engineers to develop new semiconductor manufacturing equipment and improve existing designs. Debug hardware/software interactions using schematics, datasheets, register maps, and laboratory equipment such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, DMMs, and SMUs to identify root causes of system-level issues. Evaluate interactions among software, electronics, sensors, actuators, communications, controls, and mechanical systems, using measurements and engineering evidence to characterize system behavior. Partner with New Product Introduction and Operations teams to transition equipment designs into manufacturing and use AI Assisted software engineering tools responsibly for activities such as code development, review, testing, debugging, and technical analysis. Minimum Qualifications Must be pursuing a BS or MS or equivalent experience in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related engineering field and graduate after September 2027 . Programming experience in C or C++, with familiarity working in Linux development environments and an understanding of fundamental software engineering concepts. Coursework or hands-on experience demonstrating understanding of digital and analog circuits, computer architecture, and embedded systems. Proven track record to read schematics and datasheets, plus general knowledge of oscilloscopes and DMMs. Demonstrated interest in hardware/software integration through coursework, research, personal projects, robotics, embedded systems, internships, or similar experience, including curiosity about AI Assisted software engineering tools. Preferred Qualifications Experience with embedded development tools and workflows such as Git, GCC/GNU toolchains, GDB, Make/CMake, Bash, and Linux. Hands-on experience debugging hardware/software interactions using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, or DMMs and interpreting schematics, datasheets, timing diagrams, or register maps. Experience with one or more hardware interfaces such as GPIO, SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, USB, or PCIe. Understanding of microprocessor or microcontroller architecture, including memory-mapped I/O, interrupts, registers, memory, and peripheral devices. Academic, personal, research, or internship experience involving hardware/software integration, including experience Using AI for code generation, review, testing, debugging, or technical analysis. title: Robotics Applied Scientist 2 Intern
location: Seattle, WA; North Reading, MA; NYC; Bellevue, WA; Sunnyvale, CA; Westborough, MA
description: Description Robotics Applied Scientist II Intern/Co-op (2027) Are you passionate about robotics and research? Do you want to solve real customer problems through innovative technology? Do you enjoy working on scalable research and projects in a collaborative team environment? Do you want to see your science solutions directly impact millions of customers worldwide? We’re looking for current PhD students with a passion for robotic research and applications to join us in 2027 as Robotics Applied Scientist II Interns/Co-ops to shape the future of robotics and transform automation at Amazon’s scale. By applying to this role, you will be considered for Robotics Applied Scientist II Intern/Co-op (2027) opportunities across various Robotics teams at Amazon with different robotics research focus. Internship positions are available for multiple locations, durations (3 to 6+ months), and year-round start dates (winter, spring, summer, fall). Join us at the forefront of Applied Science, where your contributions will shape the future of Robotics! Key job responsibilities As a Robotics Applied Scientist II Intern/Co-op, you will work alongside global experts to advance the state of the art in robotics and artificial intelligence, tackling innovative problems that bridge the gap between research and real-world robotics implementation to innovate and build solutions on behalf of our customers. We are particularly interested in students with specialization and expertise in one or more of the following research areas: - Robotics - Artificial Intelligence - Robotics Manipulation (e.g., robot arm, grasping, dexterous manipulation, end of arm tools/end effector) - Autonomous Mobile Robots - Mobile Manipulation - Multi-Robot Coordination - Autonomous Navigation - Locomotion - Motion/Path Planning - Controls - Perception - Sensing - Robot Learning - Machine Learning - Computer Vision - Large Language Models (LLM), Vision-Language-Action Models (VLA), Vision-Language-Models (VLM) - World Models - Human-Robot Interaction - Robotics Simulation - Optimization - And related! Key responsibilities may include: - Develop novel, scalable algorithms and/or modeling techniques that advance the state-of-the-art in science areas such as robotics, artificial intelligence, or related - Tackle challenging, innovative research problems within robotics, artificial intelligence, or related that bridge the gap between theoretical advancement and practical robotics implementation - Collaborate with cross-functional teams to solve complex problems, and to communicate research findings clearly, leveraging your expertise in robotics, artificial intelligence, or related - Demonstrate the ability to work independently, thrive in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment - Leverage AI-powered tools where applicable to accelerate research, experimentation, and prototyping. - Critically review and validate outputs from AI tools and automated systems. About the team Explore Robotics Teams at Amazon At Amazon, robotics is where innovative research meets real-world deployment. There are many different specialized robotics teams, including the few highlighted below. Learn more about Robotics at Amazon here: https://www.amazon.science/research-areas/robotics Fulfillment Technologies and Robotics We build dynamic partnerships between people and intelligent machines. This intricate collaboration helps Amazon fulfill orders with unmatched accuracy. Working in symphony with our robotic technology, you’ll have the opportunity to extend your technical capabilities by working alongside some of the industry’s most advanced technologies. This includes our fleet of autonomous mobile robots, sophisticated control software, and technologies like language perception, machine learning, object recognition, and semantic understanding of commands. These technologies help us deliver an ever-improving customer and employee experience, as well as improve the safety of our facilities. Amazon Robotics Amazon Robotics is at the epicenter of robotics innovation. We design, test, and build mobile robots and mechatronic systems. Our offices, labs, test floors, and factories are close together, which means we can design the hardware, write the code, test, build, and watch it all come to life. Our areas of focus include advancements in autonomous mobility, AI, robotic management software, and much more. Fauna Fauna is focused on building capable, safe, and genuinely delightful robots for everyday life. Fauna’s goal is simple: make robots people actually want to live and interact with everyday. Fauna develops tightly integrated hardware and software systems that make it faster, safer, and more intuitive to create real-world robotic products. Fauna’s work spans the full stack: mechanical design, control systems, dynamic modeling, and intelligent software. The focus is not just functionality, but overall experience. Amazon Fulfillment Technologies Amazon Fulfillment Technologies develops tech solutions that create network optimizations for all Amazon sites worldwide. We own network infrastructure and devices in all buildings and labor planning and scheduling technology for fulfillment centers in North America and Europe. Basic Qualifications - Are 18 years of age or older - Are enrolled in a PhD - PhD in engineering, technology, computer science, machine learning, robotics, operations research, statistics, mathematics or equivalent quantitative field - Demonstrated science depth in a specific research area, evidenced through publications, thesis work, or equivalent contributions - Relevant academic or industry research experience with state-of-the-art scientific principles and techniques in one or more science intern disciplines such as robotics, artificial intelligence, or related - Experience programming in Python, C++, or similar language Preferred Qualifications - Have publications at top-tier peer-reviewed conferences or journals - Experience with research design, development, execution while following best practices in scientific methodology - Experience inventing or adapting state-of-the art scientific approaches, models, or algorithms to solve business or customer problems - Experience with algorithm development, data structures implementation, and software development concepts and methodologies - Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to present complex technical information in a clear and concise manner to a variety of audiences - Experience implementing algorithms using modern robotics and vision toolkits (e.g. PyTorch, ROS2, Isaac Sim, OpenCV, or PCL) - Experience with AI-assisted development tools to accelerate research, coding, or evaluation Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. description: Robotics Applied Scientist II Intern/Co-op (2027) Are you passionate about robotics and research? Do you want to solve real customer problems through innovative technology? Do you enjoy working on scalable research and projects in a collaborative team environment? Do you want to see your science solutions directly impact millions of customers worldwide? We’re looking for current PhD students with a passion for robotic research and applications to join us in 2027 as Robotics Applied Scientist II Interns/Co-ops to shape the future of robotics and transform automation at Amazon’s scale. By applying to this role, you will be considered for Robotics Applied Scientist II Intern/Co-op (2027) opportunities across various Robotics teams at Amazon with different robotics research focus. Join us at the forefront of Applied Science, where your contributions will shape the future of Robotics! Key job responsibilities As a Robotics Applied Scientist II Intern/Co-op, you will work alongside global experts to advance the state of the art in robotics and artificial intelligence, tackling innovative problems that bridge the gap between research and real-world robotics implementation to innovate and build solutions on behalf of our customers. title: Project / Program Management (Eng) Intern
description: Are you a problem solver looking for a hands-on internship position with a market-leading company that will help develop your career and reward you intellectually and professionally? About Analog Devices Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI ) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and X . At ADI, you will learn from the brightest minds who are here to help you grow and succeed. During your internship, you will make an impact through work on meaningful projects alongside a team of experts. Collaborating with colleagues in an environment of respect and responsibility, you will create connections that will become a part of your professional network. ADI’s culture values aligned goals, work-life balance, continuous and life-long learning opportunities, and shared rewards. The internship program features various lunch-and-learn topics and social events with other interns and full-time employees. At ADI, our goal is to develop our interns so they are the first to be considered for full-time roles. Apply now for the opportunity to grow your career and help innovate ahead of what’s possible. As an Engineering Project Management Intern within the Advanced Cores Group (ACG), you will work alongside experienced project managers and engineers to support the development of advanced core technology and intellectual property (IP) for our Aerospace & Defense Business Unit. This internship will provide hands-on exposure to engineering project management, cross-functional collaboration, project planning, and the product development lifecycle. You will support project activities across multiple engineering disciplines and collaborate with team members at several locations globally. Through mentorship and practical experience, you will gain an understanding of how complex engineering projects are planned, coordinated, tracked, and delivered. Engineering Project Management Intern Responsibilities/Duties Cross-Functional Collaboration: Support project managers and functional teams across hardware engineering, software development, applications, manufacturing, and other disciplines in coordinating project activities. Project Planning Support : Assist with maintaining project schedules, tracking milestones and deliverables, identifying dependencies, and documenting project risks and action items. Project Tracking: Help monitor project progress against schedule, scope, and key deliverables under the guidance of project managers. Risk and Action Tracking: Assist with documenting project risks, issues, decisions, and follow-up actions to help teams stay aligned. Project Communications: Help prepare project status updates, meeting materials, presentations, and other communications for project stakeholders. Meeting Coordination: Participate in cross-functional project meetings, capture action items and decisions, and help follow up with appropriate team members. Data and Reporting: Assist with organizing and analyzing project information using tools such as Excel, PowerPoint, Jira, Confluence, or other project management systems. Process and Standards: Learn and support internal project management processes, engineering development practices, and applicable quality or industry standards. Continuous Improvement: Identify opportunities to improve project tracking, reporting, documentation, or team processes and contribute ideas to the broader ACG organization. Professional Development: Build an understanding of engineering project management while gaining exposure to technical teams, development processes, and cross-functional program execution. Minimum Qualifications Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Engineering Management, or a related technical field. Interest in engineering, technology, and project/program management. Strong interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills. Ability to collaborate effectively in a team-oriented environment. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Ability to manage multiple assignments and adapt to changing priorities. Problem-solving mindset with a willingness to learn, ask questions, and take initiative. Familiarity with Microsoft Office tools, including Excel, Word, and PowerPoint. Preferred Qualifications Coursework, academic projects, extracurricular activities, or student organization experience involving engineering, project management, or team-based technical projects. Exposure to project management or collaboration tools such as Jira, Confluence, or Microsoft Project. Familiarity with engineering development or product development lifecycles. Exposure to integrated circuit (IC), hardware, or software development through coursework, projects, or previous experience. Familiarity with RF or wireless communication concepts. Experience participating in cross-functional or multidisciplinary student/project teams. Basic exposure to scripting, data analysis, or automation tools such as Python or Excel. Strong time-management skills and an eagerness to learn in a fast-paced technical environment.
